name: expenses
about: The expense tracker from chat-grown-software, in 8 turns, in language-neutral form. Expected answers are not stored here: the simulated user computes them by running the JS reference program (bench/reference.ts) on each question.

invariants.name: expenses-shape
invariants.rule: every expense has amount: finite number > 0, category: non-empty string, and optionally note: string; no other keys

invariants.name: budgets-shape
invariants.rule: every budget value is a number >= 0

invariants.name: known-keys
invariants.rule: the state's top-level keys are only expenses and budgets (either may be absent)

turns.user: Let me record expenses: an amount and a category. Call it add_expense(amount, category).
What's my total so far? Call it total().
Break it down by category: by_category() gives a map from category to amount. The categories should always add up to the total.
turns.law: for any state, the values of by_category() sum to total() (within half a cent)

turns.user: Money should be in cents. When I add 0.10 and 0.20 the total should say 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004. Same for by_category.
turns.law: total() is always a whole number of cents

turns.user: Don't let me add an expense of zero or less, or one without a category. Throw an error.
Let me set a monthly budget per category with set_budget(category, amount), and over_budget() tells me which ones I'm over, sorted.
turns.law: every category in over_budget() has spent more than its budget

turns.user: Which category do I spend the most on? Call it top_category(). If two tie, pick the alphabetically first; with no expenses, null.
turns.law: top_category() is null or no category has spent more

turns.user: Can expenses have an optional note, like 'coffee with Sam'? add_expense(amount, category, note).
